rows.proposal_note: Coherent: unavailable is a module-local helper used only at :195, :205, :271, :293 and :330 (grep in plan-write-admission.ts), and inputBindingProblem is imported only for :329, so deleting the five branches plus the helper and the import leaves no dangling type, switch or caller. Keep the forbidden checks (:197-202, :273-283, :328), which are not covered by readExecution. Nothing reserves these duplicate facts for a later slice; the reader's own unchanged/unavailable contract (run-state-service.ts:230-264) remains the one enforcement.

rows.proposal_note: Deleting the guard and the local forbidden helper is coherent because nothing else uses it (request-facts-reader.ts:26, :80) and the four callers keep their own refusals; the rule-1/RC10 refusal before any foreign read still happens at plan-service.ts:2319-2321 and at the two boundWriteActor/identifyPlanWriter points. rows.evidence: The live route is correctly closed. The comparator at src/contracts/core/prepared-execution.ts:149 runs only when input.platformTargets has at least two entries (:148-150); platformTargets is built only for the proposal phase from undetermined platform items (src/core/agent-runtime/context-assembler.ts:1434-1440); a proposal phase is entered only from awaiting_proposal (src/core/work-graph/tasks/claim-service.ts:299; src/core/work-graph/tasks/execution-entry-service.ts:1490-1492), which itself requires a non-empty proposalTargets, i.e. process items (src/core/work-graph/state/unknown-call-review.ts:508-513, :811-813). The real Kernel runs a batch in parallel only when every call is independent read-only (vendor/coding-agent/dist/tools/registry/tool-registry.js:133-143), and recovery books outcome_unknown for the running calls and then ends the Run (vendor/coding-agent/dist/core/runtime/recovery/recovery-coordinator.js:118-141), so a crash leaves at most one non-read-only unresolved call; tests/work-graph/K3-06-mixed-kinds-owner.test.ts:6-12 records the same fact, which is why the owner-level mixed record cannot be produced by public steps. But that does not make the arm unreachable: renderUnknownCallReviewZh is also run on the manifest read from the stored envelope (execution-entry-service.ts:1049-1055), and manifestProblem never validates unknownCallReview (execution-entry-service.ts:429-491), so a hand-edited or corrupted stored manifest can carry two platformTargets and execute the comparator. That is tampering only, so the evidence supports U, not D2.
rows.proposal_note: The proposed deletion is safe because the re-sort is redundant in every platform-written manifest: buildUnknownCallReviewInputV1 already copies and sorts platformTargets (src/core/agent-runtime/context-assembler.ts:511), and aliasOf sorts the aliases before that (:1431-1436), so using input.platformTargets directly at :149 changes nothing for real data. Do not drop the surrounding platform line (:148-152): the mixed card is current spec (docs/refactor/design/orchestration-2026-10/slices/slice-K3-SPEC.md:102, :432-435, :555, :568; L20/D7) and is proven at the owner level (K3-46). Claude's optional wider deletion needs a spec change, not this cleanup.
